item.content:encoded:
the sabbaticals of Decibelles […]

I'm only on break for another couple weeks or so. It's no biggie. The important thing to remember is that real life takes precedent over this site.

Quality of the site is another topic for another time, I feel.

So I don't double-post; this is a nice tale but it doesn't feel engaging or entertaining, and the tone it carried made it a bit obvious where this would go. I was hoping Raphael was talking to no one in there, or at least a mental projection of a personality to accompany him in his bitter final moments. As obvious as that also is, it would have made for something more morally ambiguous and complex, as a man struggles to reconcile the good he believes exist in the Foundation to what he's seen and experienced. As it is, it just echos the other bleak and "no hope left" tales on the site.

One point in specific:

Raphael didn't answer. His eyes passed over his comrade to the body of a dead man laying near them. A bullet was lodged in the man's skull, and Raphael's magazine was empty.

This is way too unclear. Did that last sentence imply Raphael kill Hermes himself? Or that Raphael killed the man earlier? Because depending on the answer, that takes Raphael's character in certain directions and solidifies/establishes his views, which would make the end of the tale stronger than it is. As it is, having that ambiguity in the quote doesn't work at all.

item.content:encoded:
In light of Djoric's final story, and TwistedGears's comment in the discussion for it that the site is waning, I can't help but see this as a eulogy for someone not dead yet.

Though I know the site is not going anywhere, the departures of Djoric, djkaktus and thekillerax as well as the sabbaticals of Decibelles and thedeadlymoose have been weighing heavily on me and I can't help but feel as if I jumped on the ship as it started to sink. That's just my opinion, I could be right, I could be wrong.

All that aside, +1.

EDIT: I've realized this might be construed as stirring up controversy and trouble. None meant, I was merely offering my take on the story.
